legend: An amelanotic spindle cell tumour fills the dermis and extends into the superficial subcutis.
copyright: Elder DE, Massi D, Scolyer RA, Willemze R, editors. WHO classification of skin tumours. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2018. (WHO classification of tumours series, 4th ed.; vol. 11). https://publications.iarc.fr/560.

legend: Compact fascicles of tumour cells are present in the dermis, separated by thin strands of collagen. Some tumour cells display clear cell features.
copyright: Elder DE, Massi D, Scolyer RA, Willemze R, editors. WHO classification of skin tumours. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2018. (WHO classification of tumours series, 4th ed.; vol. 11). https://publications.iarc.fr/560.

legend: Multinucleated wreath-like giant cells are present.
copyright: Elder DE, Massi D, Scolyer RA, Willemze R, editors. WHO classification of skin tumours. Lyon (France): International Agency for Research on Cancer; 2018. (WHO classification of tumours series, 4th ed.; vol. 11). https://publications.iarc.fr/560.

legend: There is an amelanotic infiltrative spindle cell tumour involving acral skin.
Nests of tumour cells are present at the dermoepidermal junction, overlying fascicles of intradermal spindle cells, with an occasional multinucleated cell.
